transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Basically, I'm here because I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's like... I'll start talking to someone about my overnight shift at work, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or the patient charts. I don't really mean to, but I can see everyone looking at me and getting completely lost. It's just getting really hard to communicate right now.
Aside from the trouble with your speech, have you been experiencing any unusual perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't?
No, I haven't really had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's just my thoughts getting all jumbled up when I try to talk.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as periods of feeling extremely high-energy or unusually low and hopeless?

I haven't had any of that high energy, no. But... yeah, definitely the low part. Most days I just feel really heavy and empty right from the time I wake up. It's been pretty rough lately. Like, after my shifts, I'll just sit out in the parking lot in my car, just crying for a while before I can even get it together to drive home.
During the times when your mood has been at its lowest, have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled by an outside force, or that people were talking about you or plotting against you?

Yeah, it's... when the depression gets really bad, that's when I start feeling like people are against me. I get this strong feeling that the supervisors at work are watching me through the security cameras, just waiting for me to mess up. And because my mood is so low and I'm so stressed about the cameras, my speech gets even more tangled up. Like, if they actually came down to ask me what I was doing, I wouldn't even be able to explain myself clearly because my words just won't come out right.
Have there been any periods of time where you felt this intense suspicion and paranoia about people watching you, even when you weren't feeling particularly depressed or down?

Yeah, actually. There was... I guess a stretch of a few weeks not too long ago where my mood was okay. I wasn't in that deep, dark place, you know? But I still had that feeling. I still really believed the cameras were on me and the supervisors were monitoring my every move. I kept acting super guarded the whole time I was at work, even though I didn't feel depressed right then.

Looking back at the past few months, have there been any periods lasting two weeks or longer where you experienced these disorganized thoughts and feelings of being watched, while not having any symptoms of depression at all?

Yeah, like I was just saying, um... there was exactly that. It was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't in that deep, depressed place at all. My mood was actually fine. But I still completely believed the cameras were on me and that the supervisors were monitoring me. I was still acting really guarded at work the whole time. So, yeah, it was definitely at least a few weeks where I didn't have the depression, but I still had all those other thoughts going on.

During those weeks when your mood was fine, did you ever experience any other unusual beliefs, such as the idea that your thoughts were being broadcast to others or that your body was being influenced by some outside power?

No, I didn't feel like my thoughts were being broadcast or that my body was being controlled. It was really just about the supervisors. I'm sure they changed my shifts and watch me through the unit cameras to see if I'm unsafe. People at work tell me the schedule changes are just because of staffing shortages, but I know that's not true. I know they're watching me.
